items.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025
items.q: So we ended up with a G flat in the violins and David Nadien, the brilliant concertmaster for the Philharmonic and a great, great concertmaster in hundreds of sessions was laughing at me a little bit.

ctx.x: It sounds like you avoided the things that some of us have experienced, for instance your first time writing string parts and the concertmaster looks over his glasses and said, “Young man, the violin cannot play a low F sharp.”

That actually happened one time. And I was very embarrassed. But the only — I know, I know how a violin is tuned. The only reason it happened was because there was an arrangement and someone at the last minute demanded that it be transposed down a semi- tone. So we ended up with a G flat in the violins and David Nadien, the brilliant concertmaster for the Philharmonic and a great, great concertmaster in hundreds of sessions was laughing at me a little bit. He knew that I knew better. He said, “Rob, Rob, we are…
And you probably resisted saying, “It’s not my fault, I know better.”
